mechanism: Complete cereal crop activities must fit both total annual listed field work and their reaping subset, using the same reference workforce. Fixed rural food claims precede export; the remaining grain changes civilian and institutional allocations and therefore available reach sources.

sources.title: Columella, De re rustica 2.12.1–2
sources.access: Primary English translation, cached chapter 12 text and earlier checked transcription read
sources.used_for: Retain listed wheat/barley field-task totals and reaping subsets to the threshing floor. Normative estate advice, not universal actual labour productivity.

sources.title: FAO Farm Management for Asia, chapter 9
sources.access: Primary cached manual's seasonal planning and resource-constraint sections read
sources.used_for: Apply simultaneous whole-activity land/work constraints. Does not supply ancient household workforce shares or calendars.

scenario_assumptions: 40% workers within an explicit reference rural food group; 300/600 already allocated listed field hours per worker per year; 10/30 reaping days; 8-hour conversion day and approximate 0.25 ha/iugerum. These are sensitivity budgets, not historical demographic estimates.
not_inferred: Actual household composition, total subsistence work, leisure, hired labour, labour transfers between cells, draft-animal support, other task deadlines, historical reaping dates, famine, institutions or technological development.
controls: The same crop, fixed rural demand, cell assignment, collection, stores and transport; all six earlier food/reference cases and masks remain exactly unchanged. Compare matched annual hours with different reaping windows, and matched reaping windows with different annual hours.
